candidate.title: NG Cap- / ture-C
candidate.scope: Single linear NG Capture-C row of the assigned Illumina poster, identified by the wrapped card label NG Cap-/ture-C and the caption Next-generation Capture-C (NG Capture-C). The independently checked catalogue heading targets the same assay. The graph records the nine depicted operations through an enriched indexed DNA endpoint. Neighbouring Hi-C/3-C/Capture-C, ChIA-PET and 4-C graphics are separate context, not alternative targets. NG Capture-C and Next-Generation Capture-C are an abbreviation and expansion of this one target; embedded 3C library preparation is a component. Davies et al. (PMID 26595209) resolve this as a targeted biotinylated-DNA-oligo capture implementation with sequential capture rounds. The drawing compresses the full implementation: it depicts one capture pass and one pre-hybridization PCR arrow, without explicit sample pooling, post-capture PCR, repeat capture, sequencing or analysis nodes. The primary-paper distinctions are recorded without adding those unshown routes or claiming equivalence to all Capture-C family implementations. The catalogue also cites Duan et al. (reference 309, 3C-Seq) and Lieberman-Aiden et al. (reference 310, Hi-C) as background context; their primary content was not supplied or inspected, and neither is treated as an NG Capture-C method paper.

states.label: Enriched indexed DNA library: schematic DNA endpoint
features: The rightmost icon is short linear DNA with colored adapter-end segments; it omits the bead and bait and does not specify release or recovery chemistry.
Selection is mediated by biotinylated bait bound to streptavidin, enriching DNA associated with the chosen viewpoints while background and noninformative fragments can remain.

Sequencing junction-bearing genomic DNA can associate a captured restriction fragment with its ligated partner; the resulting interaction profile is a relative representation of contacts recorded in the 3C library, not a direct measurement of geometric distance or proof of regulatory causality.
Sample indexes identify prepared libraries; the contact association is carried by genomic ligation junctions, not by the indexes or by sequencing the protein scaffold.
Sequencing and computational filtering are described by the paper but are not drawn as downstream operations here.

method_scopes.rationale: All nine operations belong to the single NG Capture-C route, with the exact drawn preparation histories retained. There is no depicted retained branch or cross-row transfer. The family wording in the catalogue does not make nearby method rows alternative targets. Full-text Davies Figure 1a independently supports the fixation/digestion/ligation/extraction, sonication, indexed-library, bait and streptavidin interfaces. Its pooling and repeated capture/PCR extend beyond this simplified row and are disclosed as the paper-supported interpretation of the endpoint, not inserted into the graph. The yellow ligation symbol has no assigned chemistry; biotinylation is explicitly on the capture bait.

checks.rationale: Independent image and source checks support the candidate at its declared single-row schematic scope. All nine labeled transformations, twelve material states and twenty material routes are represented. The only two multi-input operations are genuine bait hybridization and affinity attachment, not collapsed independent processing. Junction DNA remains the contact carrier; indexed fragments, bait biotin and the capture support have distinct roles. The beadless endpoint is explicitly schematic, with primary-paper PCR-from-beads/repeated capture disclosed rather than an invented elution. No additional target workflow or retained branch is visible, and the unassigned yellow symbol does not require a chemical claim to interpret this architecture.
